subject: medicine
title: Parasitic and helminthic infections: intestinal, tissue and blood

steps.tx: Ask about **amoebiasis** when a patient reports bloody mucoid stools with tenesmus, and about liver abscess when fever follows dysentery with pain in the right shoulder. Ask about **giardiasis** when stools are frothy and bulky with weight loss from malabsorption. Ask about **filariasis** when the legs swell or a hydrocele appears, and about kala azar when fever persists for weeks with wasting and a huge spleen. Ask about barefoot soil exposure and pork consumption.
steps.say: Take a careful history because the story usually points to the parasite. Ask about bloody mucoid stools with tenesmus, which suggest amoebic dysentery, and about right shoulder pain with fever after dysentery, which suggests amoebic liver abscess. Ask about frothy bulky stools with weight loss, which suggest giardiasis with malabsorption. Ask about swollen legs or a new hydrocele, which suggest filariasis, and about prolonged fever with wasting, which suggests kala azar. Ask about walking barefoot on soil and about eating pork.

steps.tx: Examine the abdomen for a tender enlarged liver in amoebic abscess and for a huge soft spleen with generalised nodes in kala azar. Examine the **lymphatic system** when the legs are swollen and when a chylous hydrocele transilluminates, since filariasis blocks drainage. Look for pallor with koilonychia in hookworm **anaemia** and for itchy migratory skin tracks in larva migrans. Order bedside **stool microscopy** for ova and cysts, night blood films for microfilariae, and urine inspection for milky chyluria.
steps.say: Examine the abdomen for a tender liver edge, which supports amoebic abscess, and for a huge soft spleen with firm generalised nodes, which supports kala azar. Examine swollen legs for pitting and a hydrocele for transillumination with milky fluid, which support filariasis. Look for pallor with spoon shaped nails, which suggests hookworm anaemia, and for itchy winding skin tracks, which suggest larva migrans. Send stool for microscopy to look for ova and cysts, examine night blood for microfilariae, and inspect urine for milky chyluria.

steps.tx: This panel shows three helminth ova side by side with their defining features labelled. The **Ascaris egg** carries a rough mammillated coat, the hookworm ovum has a thin shell holding a cleaved dark morula, and the **Trichuris egg** is barrel shaped with clear bipolar plugs. Recognising these shapes matters because **stool microscopy** remains the bedside test that confirms intestinal helminth infection and guides deworming.
steps.say: Look closely at this panel because it shows exactly what you must recognise under the microscope. The Ascaris egg on the left carries a rough mammillated coat that looks like a thick brown shell. The hookworm egg in the middle has a thin clear shell holding a dark berry like cluster of cells. The Trichuris egg on the right is barrel shaped with a clear plug at each pole. When you see these shapes in stool samples, you can confirm the worm and choose the right deworming drug.

steps.tx: Confirm the diagnosis with triple stool samples examined for ova and parasites, and support amoebic disease with serology and pus examination showing anchovy sauce material. Confirm hydatid disease with imaging that shows daughter cysts, filariasis with night blood films, and kala azar with rK39 testing or splenic aspirate. Note blood **eosinophilia** as a flag for tissue helminth infection and use scans to stage cysts. Separate amoebic abscess from **pyogenic abscess**, nodal disease from tuberculosis, cysts from **tumour**, and bloody stools from inflammatory bowel disease.
steps.say: Confirm the diagnosis with three stool samples examined for ova and parasites on microscopy. Support amoebic disease with serology and examine any drained pus for anchovy sauce material. Confirm hydatid disease with imaging that shows daughter cysts, confirm filariasis with night blood films, and confirm kala azar with rapid antibody testing or splenic aspirate. Blood eosinophilia acts as a flag for tissue helminth infection, so obtain scans to stage cysts. Separate amoebic abscess from bacterial abscess, nodal disease from tuberculosis, cysts from tumour, and bloody stools from inflammatory bowel disease.

vis.alt: CT or MRI scan of the brain showing multiple ring-enhancing lesions and some calcified cysts, indicative of neurocysticercosis.
vis.caption: Brain imaging revealing cysticercosis: ring-enhancing and calcified lesions. Image: Vasileios Ntoukas, Dennis Tappe, Daniel Pfütze, Michaela Simon, and Th, CC0/PD, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Treat amoebiasis with **metronidazole** followed by a luminal agent, soil transmitted worms with albendazole, and flukes and tapeworms with **praziquantel**. Treat filariasis with diethylcarbamazine while watching for reactions, and kala azar with liposomal amphotericin. Remove hydatid cysts surgically with scolicidal precautions, correct iron deficiency and control seizures, and prevent reinfection with footwear, clean pork and bed nets. Never give steroids alone for cysticercal oedema, never give diethylcarbamazine in loa loa infection, and never rupture a **hydatid cyst**.
steps.say: Treat amoebiasis with metronidazole followed by a luminal agent that clears cysts from the gut. Treat soil transmitted worms with albendazole and treat flukes and tapeworms with praziquantel. Give diethylcarbamazine for filariasis while you watch for reactions, and give liposomal amphotericin for kala azar. Remove hydatid cysts surgically with scolicidal precautions, correct iron deficiency, control seizures, and prevent reinfection with footwear, safe pork and bed nets. Never give steroids alone for brain swelling in cysticercosis, never give diethylcarbamazine in loa loa infection, and never rupture a hydatid cyst.
